hotspot_events.title: MOFCOM Announces Extension of Rare Earth Export Control Suspension to 2027-01-10
hotspot_events.heat_reason: The cliff is pushed back by two months but not lifted; combined with a package of US tariff and port fee extensions, this directly impacts the decision window for the magnet steel/motor supply chain
hotspot_events.summary: MOFCOM announced on Nov 9 that the suspension period for six Oct 9, 2025 rare earth export control announcements is extended to 2027-01-10 (continuing the suspension from Nov 11 to Jan 10, 2027), pushing the cliff back by two months; bundled extensions include: extending the suspension of additional 24% tariffs on the US by another two months, and extending the suspension of special port fees for US-flagged vessels to 2027-01-10; the licensing system for 7 types of medium and heavy rare earths from April 2025 was never suspended and remains continuously in effect.
numbers: Six announcements remaining suspended from 11-11 to 2027-01-10
Suspension of 24% US tariffs extended by another two months

hotspot_events.title: Copper Prices Rebound on Monday; Spot Market Sets New Record Tightness
hotspot_events.heat_reason: Futures rebounded, but both spot premium and import premium hit record highs. The growing divergence between futures and spot markets increases misjudgment risk, directly affecting copper price-locking decisions
hotspot_events.summary: LME 3M closed at $13,880/ton (+0.81%) on 11-09, after last Friday's 13,768 marked the lowest close since late July; Yangshan copper premium hit a record $230/ton, Shanghai spot premium reached a record 2,615 RMB/ton, and SHFE inventory at 33,848 tons was the lowest in nearly three years—a futures rebound does not equal spot market relief.

hotspot_events.title: Section 301 Exclusion Extension Applies Starting Today
hotspot_events.heat_reason: 178 exclusion extensions apply starting today, directly determining the import cost for goods cleared through customs from today; Federal Register publication remains pending confirmation, leaving a formal procedural risk
hotspot_events.summary: Two USTR notices on Nov 6 (178 exclusions + maritime fee suspension) extended to 2027-01-09, applying to goods customs cleared/withdrawn from warehouse starting 11-10 00:01; Federal Register publication remains unconfirmed as of this morning's search (a precedent occurred last year where publication lagged behind the effective date, after which it was applied retroactively).

industry_updates.title: Ministry of Commerce announces rare-earth control suspension extended to 2027-01-10, with the 24% U.S. tariff and U.S.-flagged vessel port fees also extended by two months
industry_updates.detail: The six announcements from 2025-10-09 have their suspension period extended from 11-11 to 2027-01-10; the suspension of the 24% tariff on the U.S. is further extended by two months (effective from 11-10 13:01), and the special port fee for U.S.-flagged vessels is extended to 2027-01-10; the licensing regime for seven medium-to-heavy rare earths issued in 2025-04 has never been suspended and remains in effect.
